issues.contract_item: "#F5841E" ... "source": ".claude/gauntlet/originals/user/circletel-product-development/references/house_standards.md line 45", "evidence": "A one-digit variant matching neither of the main two. Appears in no production file. Assessed as a transcription error."
issues.evidence_from_original: app/layout.tsx line 81: `themeColor: '#F5841E', // CircleTel Orange (official)`. Independent grep: `grep -rioE 'F5841E' app components lib` returns 50 occurrences (e.g. app/(marketing)/check-coverage/CheckCoverageContent.tsx lines 99, 131, 210, 260 as CTA fills; app/admin/marketing/announcements/page.tsx default bg_color). Pillow sampling of .design/logos/LOGO-01/02/06 gives the mark's orange as #F6841F — #F5841E is within one unit per channel of the artwork, the same closeness the contract credits to #F5831F.
issues.why_it_matters: The contract's rank-1 quality is 'factual exactness', and its single most load-bearing new finding is the artwork-vs-token orange split. It erases a fourth live orange that (a) ships 50 times, (b) is annotated 'CircleTel Orange (official)' in the root layout, and (c) is as faithful a transcription of the trademark as the value the contract defends. An implementation built on this contract will assert #F5841E is a typo that appears nowhere, which is false, and will mis-scope the escalation the contract's whole orange analysis rests on. The PWA theme colour is also the browser-chrome colour on every mobile page load — not a marginal usage.
issues.recommended_fix: Replace the #F5841E entry with: "value": "#F5841E", "source": "app/layout.tsx line 81 viewport themeColor, annotated 'CircleTel Orange (official)'; house_standards.md line 45; 50 literal occurrences across app/, components/ and lib/ including marketing CTA fills", "evidence": "A fourth live orange, within one unit per channel of the logo artwork's #F6841F — as faithful a transcription of the mark as #F5831F. Not a transcription error. It is the PWA/browser-chrome colour on every page." and add it to the escalated orange question rather than dismissing it.

issues.contract_item: success_looks_like[1]: "The values it states match the values the production design tokens actually define; a divergence between the guideline and the shipped product is a failure of this capability, not an acceptable variance."
issues.evidence_from_original: The same contract states, in contested_facts: "SPLIT AND UNRESOLVED BY EVIDENCE ... the logo's own #F6841F (of which the skill's #F5831F is a faithful transcription) is authoritative for the mark itself", and in constraints: "Where the repository's brand sources disagree on a fact, the disagreement must be reported with both values and their provenance, not silently resolved." Independently verified: the mark's orange (#F6841F, dominant opaque pixel of LOGO-01 at 614,613 px and LOGO-06 at 3,866,803 px) exists in no Tailwind token; `grep -rioE 'F6841F' app components lib` returns 0.
issues.why_it_matters: This success criterion makes token divergence a failure without qualification, so a capability that correctly reports the mark's own #F6841F, or correctly names Arial for an email template, is graded as failing by the contract's own top-line criterion while simultaneously being required by contract constraints. A judge scoring against success_looks_like will penalise exactly the behaviour contested_facts demands. It also silently converts the escalated business question into a decided one in favour of the tokens.
issues.recommended_fix: Replace with: "For any fact the production design tokens govern — web and product-UI colour and type, and the resolved value of any named token — the values it states match those tokens exactly; a divergence there is a failure, not an acceptable variance. For facts the tokens do not govern — the mark's own colours, print, email and generated imagery — it states the artwork or medium-specific value and flags that no production token applies."

issues.contract_item: objective_invariants: "TYPEFACE AGREEMENT — ... the `next/font/google` imports in /home/user/circletel/app/layout.tsx and the `fontFamily` map in tailwind.config.ts must contain every typeface the capability names, and the capability must name no typeface absent from both." and contested_facts: "Arial is loaded nowhere in production ... Verified absent."
issues.evidence_from_original: `grep -rn 'Arial' app components lib` returns 18 live sites, and they are the shipped non-web media the contract claims to serve: lib/notifications/templates/base-wrapper.ts line 17 and base-template.ts line 41 (`font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif;` — the shared wrapper for every transactional email); components/admin/quotes/QuotePreview.tsx lines 74, 88, 91 (quote document, with wordmark text at fill #F5831F); app/api/quotes/business/[id]/email/route.ts line 142; app/api/admin/billing/send-emandate-reminder/route.ts line 139; lib/payment/netcash-webhook-processor.ts (4 sites). Arial is absent only from the *web app's* font loading (layout.tsx next/font, tailwind fontFamily, globals.css).
issues.why_it_matters: The contract's rank-4 quality is consumer-neutrality and it explicitly lists email and print as consumers. Email clients cannot rely on webfonts, which is why Arial is the deliberate choice there — it is not stale placeholder text in that medium. As written, the invariant forbids the capability from naming the typeface that email and quote documents actually ship, and the flat claim 'loaded nowhere in production' is false. It undercuts the contract's own consumer-neutrality argument at the one point where it is tested.
issues.recommended_fix: Rewrite as: "TYPEFACE AGREEMENT — for the web and product-UI surface, the typefaces named must be exactly those app/layout.tsx imports from next/font/google and tailwind.config.ts maps: Manrope (display/headings), Inter (body/UI/data), JetBrains Mono (technical). For email and document media, where webfonts cannot be relied on, the shipped fallback is Arial/Helvetica (lib/notifications/templates/base-wrapper.ts, base-template.ts, components/admin/quotes/QuotePreview.tsx); naming it there is correct, naming it for the web surface is not." And correct the contested_facts evidence line to "Arial is absent from the web app's font loading but is the deliberate shipped typeface in email templates and quote documents (18 sites)."

issues.contract_item: objective_invariants PRODUCTION COLOUR TOKENS / PRODUCTION COLOUR ROLES — no mention of an information/link blue, of #FEF3E8, or of #D96F1A anywhere in the contract (string counts: 3B82F6 = 0, FEF3E8 = 0, D96F1A = 0).
issues.evidence_from_original: SKILL.md Extended Palette: "| **Orange Light** | `#FEF3E8` | Hover states, light backgrounds |", "| **Orange Dark** | `#D96F1A` | Pressed states, shadows |", "| **Info Blue** | `#3B82F6` | Information, links |". Independently verified: #3B82F6 has 37 literal occurrences in app/components/lib (a live production value the contract's own authority rule would endorse); #FEF3E8 and #D96F1A have 0.
issues.why_it_matters: Three brand facts the user carries in the original are dropped without trace. Info Blue is the worst case: it is a real original brand value that production corroborates 37 times, and the contract neither carries it nor records it as contested — a straight loss of a fact. #FEF3E8 and #D96F1A are silently superseded by #FDF2E9 and #C45A30, which is precisely the 'silently resolve a disagreement' behaviour the contract's own constraints and never_do list forbid.
issues.recommended_fix: Add to PRODUCTION COLOUR ROLES: "info blue #3B82F6 — informational callouts and links; 37 literal occurrences in production; carried from the original extended palette." Add a contested_facts entry: "The orange tint and shade — original #FEF3E8 / #D96F1A versus production circleTel orange-light #FDF2E9 / orange-dark #C45A30; the original values have zero production occurrences and are assessed superseded, recorded here rather than dropped."

issues.contract_item: objective_invariants "PRODUCTION TYPE SCALE (DESIGN.md) — h1 3.75rem/60px ... label 0.875rem/14px, 600, 1.25; mono 0.875rem/14px, 400." (the only type scale in the contract)
issues.evidence_from_original: SKILL.md Text Styles table: "Hero headline 48-64px / 800 / Dark Neutral; Section heading 32-40px / 700; Subheading 20-24px / 600; Body 16px / 400; Caption 14px / 400 / Gray; **Price 24-32px / 700 / Orange**", and Font Weights table including "800 | font-extrabold | Hero text, major headlines". The contract contains no 'price' text style and the string 'extrabold' appears zero times.
issues.why_it_matters: The original's scale is the *imagery* scale — px sizes for generated assets and a dedicated Price style, which is the single most repeated element in CircleTel social creative (the original's own worked example is "Price callout 'From R599/mo'"). Substituting DESIGN.md's rem-based web scale, which has no price token, leaves the image-generation consumer with no guidance on the one element the brand renders most. The 800 weight is also lost (defensibly — Manrope is loaded only at 600/700 — but the loss should be recorded, not silent).
issues.recommended_fix: Add an invariant: "IMAGERY TYPE SCALE (original, medium-scoped to generated assets and collateral) — hero headline 48–64px bold; section heading 32–40px; subheading 20–24px semibold; body 16px; caption 14px in grey; PRICE callout 24–32px bold in the brand orange. Note that production loads Manrope at 600/700 only, so the original's 800 weight has no shipped equivalent and resolves to 700."

issues.contract_item: constraints: "Any price, speed, coverage or contractual claim rendered into an image must be verified against the current live offer, be legible at thumbnail size, and carry whatever qualifier the offer requires — or be overlaid as real text rather than generated."
issues.evidence_from_original: Nothing in SKILL.md or references/quick-reference.md addresses claim verification, live-offer checking, qualifiers or thumbnail legibility. The contract itself puts the opposite in scope_out: "Copywriting, messaging strategy, campaign concepting, offer construction, pricing decisions and claim substantiation."
issues.why_it_matters: An invented obligation that the contract's own scope boundary excludes. It is also uncheckable by the capability — 'the current live offer' is not a repository fact any brand definition can resolve — so it will either be ignored or will force an implementation to fabricate an offer-verification step it has no source for. The contract elsewhere forbids exactly this ('Never silently invent a brand rule to fill a gap and present it as established').
issues.recommended_fix: Delete the constraint. If the legibility half is wanted, keep only the brand-owned part: "Text rendered into an image must remain legible at thumbnail size, and any commercial figure should be overlaid as real text rather than generated, since models mis-render digits." Move claim verification to open_questions_for_user.

issues.contract_item: The entire "unresolved_or_decided" array (10 items, e.g. "Extractor_1 and extractor_3 both framed the capability around image generation ... Extractor_2 argued ...") and the first-person reasoning inside contested_facts ("None of the three extractors sampled the logo artwork. I did"; "VERIFIED at synthesis time"; "Correcting extractor_1, which asserted lightNeutral was unused"), plus per-line citations such as ".claude/skills/brand-design/SKILL.md lines 65, 83, 127, 154, 168, 194, 216, 235, 251, 300, 383".
issues.evidence_from_original: None — this is metadata about how the contract was produced, not about what the user needs. The original skill contains no such material.
issues.why_it_matters: Three problems. (1) It hands a judge a line-numbered map of the reference implementation, so an implementation that happens to reproduce the original's structure is identifiable, and one that solves the same job differently is not. (2) It publishes the synthesiser's preferred conclusions as adjudicated ('Extractor_2's framing adopted'), steering any judge toward that one reading rather than toward the user's outcome. (3) Process narration is not an outcome and does not belong in an outcome contract; it inflates the document by roughly a third with material no implementation can satisfy or violate.
issues.recommended_fix: Delete "unresolved_or_decided" entirely. In contested_facts, strip first-person and extractor references from every "reasoning" field, and replace SKILL.md line-number citations with medium-neutral provenance (e.g. "the brand guideline document" / "the production Tailwind config"). Keep the substantive evidence (usage counts, pixel samples, contrast ratios); drop who found it and when.

issues.contract_item: objective_invariants "ICON SYSTEM — Phosphor via react-icons/pi ... Production-critical icons hosted locally under components/icons/ (SVG-as-JSX) or public/icons/, preserving official geometry and colours, with the Iconify identifier, source URL, icon-set licence and attribution recorded in a source comment." plus the matching constraint.
issues.evidence_from_original: Not present anywhere in the brand-design skill. It is imported wholesale from a separate project rule (.claude/rules/icon-system.md). The contract's own scope_out already says: "Choosing or authoring interface icons beyond deferring to the established Phosphor/Iconify system."
issues.why_it_matters: Implementation mechanics of a different capability (which npm package, which directory, what comment format) smuggled into a brand-identity contract as an invariant. It is not a brand fact, it is not this capability's to own, and the contract elsewhere explicitly cedes it. Its presence would let a judge reward an implementation for reciting another rule file.
issues.recommended_fix: Replace the ICON SYSTEM invariant with a single line: "ICON SYSTEM — interface iconography is governed by the project's established Phosphor/Iconify rule, not by this capability; brand styling must not override it." Delete the corresponding constraint's implementation detail, keeping only "Third-party and partner logos are outside the CircleTel brand definition and require licence and trademark checks before use."

issues.contract_item: open_questions_for_user: "GRADIENT SPECIFICATION — 'orange gradient' appears throughout the guidance with no defined stops, direction or second colour, so every asset invents its own. What is the approved gradient?"
issues.evidence_from_original: tailwind.config.ts backgroundImage defines eleven named gradient presets with explicit stops and directions, including `gradient-hero: linear-gradient(135deg, #E87A1E 0%, #1B2A4A 100%)`, `gradient-cta: linear-gradient(135deg, #E87A1E 0%, #D76026 100%)`, `gradient-cta-hover`, `gradient-card-orange: linear-gradient(135deg, #FDF2E9 0%, #FFF5EB 100%)`, `gradient-section-dark: linear-gradient(180deg, #1B2A4A 0%, #0F1427 100%)`. DESIGN.md adds the governing rule: "Don't use decorative gradients on body sections — reserve for hero backgrounds only."
issues.why_it_matters: The contract escalates as unanswerable a question its own authority rule already answers from the file it calls authoritative. It burns a user decision on something the repository defines, and loses a real, checkable production fact that generated imagery could adopt directly.
issues.recommended_fix: Move to objective_invariants: "PRODUCTION GRADIENTS (tailwind.config.ts) — hero 135deg #E87A1E→#1B2A4A; hero-light 135deg #FDF2E9→#E8F0FF; hero-dark 135deg #1B2A4A→#0F1427; CTA 135deg #E87A1E→#D76026; card-orange 135deg #FDF2E9→#FFF5EB; section-dark 180deg #1B2A4A→#0F1427. DESIGN.md restricts decorative gradients to hero backgrounds." Narrow the open question to: "do generated-image gradients adopt these UI stops, or the logo-orange lineage?"

issues.contract_item: open_questions_for_user: "DARK MODE — the palette has no dark-surface tokens, no dark-mode orange treatment ... Is dark mode in the brand's scope, and if so what are the values?"
issues.evidence_from_original: app/globals.css defines a complete `.dark` block (--background oklch(0.2046 0 0), --card oklch(0.2686 0 0), --primary oklch(0.7686 0.1647 70.0804) i.e. #F59E0B, and the full sidebar/chart scale), and tailwind.config.ts sets `darkMode: ["class"]`.
issues.why_it_matters: Dark-surface tokens do exist; the actual defect is different and more useful — they are generic shadcn scaffolding carrying the third orange (#F59E0B) into dark mode, so a dark theme currently renders amber, not CircleTel orange. Stating 'no dark tokens' misdirects the user away from the real problem.
issues.recommended_fix: Rewrite as: "DARK MODE — a full `.dark` token set exists in app/globals.css and darkMode is class-based, but it is generic shadcn scaffolding: its --primary is the amber #F59E0B, not a CircleTel orange, and no brand rule states which logo variant applies to a dark UI theme as distinct from a dark photograph. Should the dark palette be brought onto the brand orange, and what is the dark-theme logo rule?"

issues.contract_item: constraints: "South African market context governs people, settings, props, language and cultural cues in any depictive asset, operationalised concretely (realistic demographic mix, plausible local settings, local vehicles/signage/plug types) rather than asserted as a slogan."
issues.evidence_from_original: SKILL.md says only: "Specify South African context: For lifestyle/people images", "South African market appropriate", and "South African representation if showing people". No demographic, vehicle, signage or plug-type guidance exists.
issues.why_it_matters: The parenthetical is fabricated specificity presented as a constraint. 'Realistic demographic mix' in particular is an editorial decision only the brand owner can set, and enumerating props (plug types, vehicles) narrows the visual field in a way no source authorises — it also nudges every implementation toward the same literal depiction checklist, which is a mild style bias.
issues.recommended_fix: Replace with: "South African market context governs people, settings, props and cultural cues in any depictive asset; the original states this as a requirement without operational detail, so the concrete depiction checklist is a derivation and must be labelled as one, not applied as an established rule." Move the specifics to open_questions_for_user.

issues.contract_item: objective_invariants MEASURED CONTRAST: "Consequence: no orange in the palette may carry white text as normal-size body text, semantic red and green are fills/icons with dark labels rather than text colours ..."
issues.evidence_from_original: DESIGN.md components front-matter: `button-primary: backgroundColor "{colors.primary}" (#E87A1E), textColor "{colors.surface}" (#FFFFFF), typography "{typography.label}" (0.875rem/14px, 600)`, and the Components section: "Primary Button — Orange fill, white text". 14px semibold is normal-size text under WCAG, so the shipped, specified primary button is white-on-orange at the 2.90:1 the contract computes.
issues.why_it_matters: The measured ratios themselves are correct and I reproduced them; the 'Consequence' is a derived rule that the source the contract calls authoritative contradicts in its own component spec. Stated in objective_invariants it reads as an established brand rule that would fail the shipped primary button, and the contract elsewhere requires derivations to be labelled as derivations. As written it is not checkable without first resolving which of the two DESIGN.md statements wins.
issues.recommended_fix: Split the invariant. Keep the measured ratios as the invariant. Move the consequence to a labelled derivation: "DERIVED, NOT ESTABLISHED — the ratios imply white-on-orange fails AA at normal size, yet DESIGN.md's own button-primary specifies orange fill with white 14px/600 labels. This conflict is unresolved; report it rather than enforcing either side. #AE5B16 as the only orange for text on white IS established (DESIGN.md Do list)."

issues.contract_item: Usage counts presented as verified fact: "circleTel-navy appears 884 times"; "circleTel-lightNeutral has 164 uses"; "232 literal occurrences of F5831F"; "The Tailwind class circleTel-orange appears 2,743 times".
issues.evidence_from_original: My independent counts over app/ and components/: circleTel-navy 889 (not 884); circleTel-lightNeutral 163 (not 164); circleTel-orange 3081 total, of which 226 -dark, 61 -light, 48 -accessible, leaving 2746 bare (not 2743). F5831F 232 and E87A1E 200 reproduce exactly; darkNeutral 0 reproduces exactly; AE5B16 12, 747474 7, 1B2A4A 148 all reproduce exactly.
issues.why_it_matters: The counts are substantially right and none of the conclusions drawn from them change. But they are stated as exact verified figures inside a document whose rank-1 quality is factual exactness, and they are the sole basis for the darkNeutral-retire / lightNeutral-keep distinction. Small unreproducible numbers invite a judge to treat the whole evidence base as approximate.
issues.recommended_fix: State counts as approximate with the command that produced them, e.g. "circleTel-navy ≈ 885–890 occurrences in app/ and components/ (grep -roE); circleTel-lightNeutral ≈ 163; bare circleTel-orange ≈ 2,745 excluding the -dark/-light/-accessible variants."

issues.contract_item: objective_invariants COMPOSITING DEFAULTS — "logo scaled to approximately 20% of the base image width ... alpha preserved, aspect ratio preserved, high-quality resampling, default variant LOGO-01." (no output format stated)
issues.evidence_from_original: SKILL.md Integration section: "Save as JPEG: Always use `.jpg` extension (Gemini returns JPEG)"; the PIL example ends `background.convert("RGB").save("final-branded.jpg", quality=95)`; .design/scripts/add-logo.py line 89 confirms `save(output_path, "JPEG", quality=95)`. Also dropped: "Default to Flash model for iteration, Pro for text-heavy designs."
issues.why_it_matters: The JPEG-at-quality-95 output convention is a durable asset fact — it is what the shipped compositor does and what every file in .design/images/ is — not provider mechanics. Dropping it while keeping the 20%/3%/bottom-right defaults from the same paragraph is inconsistent, and an implementation writing PNGs would silently break the established asset set. (The model-choice guidance is correctly scoped out as provider mechanics.)
issues.recommended_fix: Append to COMPOSITING DEFAULTS: "...high-quality resampling, default variant LOGO-01, output written as JPEG at quality 95 (the format every asset under .design/images/ uses and the compositor emits)."

faithfulness_verdict: NO — not faithful as written, though the failure is one of overreach and two hard fact errors rather than wholesale infidelity. What it gets right is substantial and I verified it independently: the eight-variant logo set and filenames, the anatomy, the clearspace rule ('TEL' height), the 32px/10mm minimums, the composite-don't-generate prohibition, the asset-geometry table, the compositing defaults (20% / 3% / bottom-right / LOGO-01 / quality 95, all confirmed against .design/scripts/add-logo.py), the output tree, and the mood/avoid list are all carried across intact. The artwork sampling is real (#F6841F at 614,613 px in LOGO-01, 3,866,803 px in LOGO-06; #757474 grey) and is the contract's most valuable contribution. The usage counts reproduce to within ~0.2%. But it fails on three axes. (1) Fact errors at the exact points it claims most authority: #F5841E is declared absent from production when it ships 50 times and is labelled 'CircleTel Orange (official)' in app/layout.tsx (A1); Arial is declared 'loaded nowhere in production' when it is the deliberate typeface of every transactional email and quote document (A3); two open questions escalate things the repository already answers (A9, A10). (2) Dropped brand facts the user values: Info Blue #3B82F6 (37 production uses) vanishes entirely, #FEF3E8/#D96F1A are silently superseded contrary to the contract's own report-the-conflict rule, and the original's imagery type scale — including the Price-in-orange style that is the most-rendered element in CircleTel social creative — is replaced by a web scale that has no equivalent (A4, A5). (3) Invented and imported obligations: live-offer claim verification (which the contract's own scope_out excludes), the icon-system implementation detail, and the fabricated South African depiction checklist (A6, A8, A11). Fix A1, A2, A3, A4 and A5 and the contract becomes faithful; the rest are tightening.
would_rig_benchmark: YES, in two specific ways, both fixable by deletion. First, the 'unresolved_or_decided' array and the first-person reasoning inside 'contested_facts' narrate the contract's own construction — naming extractor_1/2/3, recording which framing was 'adopted', and stating 'I verified' / 'VERIFIED at synthesis time'. That is not an outcome any implementation can satisfy; it is a transcript of adjudication, and a judge reading it is told in advance which of the competing readings to reward. Second, contested_facts cites the reference implementation by file and line number — '.claude/skills/brand-design/SKILL.md lines 65, 83, 127, 154, 168, 194, 216, 235, 251, 300, 383', 'references/quick-reference.md line 8', 'SKILL.md line 96'. An implementation that mirrors the original document's structure becomes identifiable as the reference; one that serves the same user outcome with different organisation does not match the map. There is a third, milder bias: the contract's success_looks_like and TYPEFACE/TOKEN AGREEMENT invariants push unconditionally toward the production-token answer (#E87A1E, Manrope/Inter, no Arial) while contested_facts says the orange is unresolved and the email consumer genuinely ships Arial — so an implementation that correctly reports the marketing lineage or the email typeface scores worse than one that flattens everything to Tailwind. That is a thumb on the scale for one substantive position in a question the contract itself calls open. No stylistic rigging: the aesthetic register carried forward (modern, clean, professional, no neon, no clip-art) is the original's own language, not the auditor's or a house style.
authority_verdict: PARTIALLY CORRECT — right for two fact classes, wrong for three, and stated far too broadly. Where it is right: (a) if the capability names a Tailwind token it must state the value that token actually resolves to, full stop — the original's claim that circleTel-orange = #F5831F is simply false against the config and is the contract's single most urgent and most defensible correction; (b) for the web and product-UI surface, tailwind.config.ts + DESIGN.md + app/globals.css genuinely are authoritative, and I confirmed the evidence — circleTel-navy ≈889 uses versus circleTel-darkNeutral 0, the config's own 'Legacy aliases (for backwards compatibility)' comment on darkNeutral/lightNeutral, DESIGN.md naming #1B2A4A 'the authority color', app/layout.tsx line 149 carrying bg-[#F9FAFB] on <body>, and layout.tsx line 5 importing exactly Inter/Manrope/JetBrains_Mono with Arial absent from all web font loading. Navy over #1F2937 and Manrope/Inter over Arial for screens are correct calls, and #AE5B16 is a genuine production-approved value the original omits. Where it is wrong: (1) THE MARK. Tailwind tokens have no authority over the trademark's own colours. I sampled the artwork independently: LOGO-01 and LOGO-06 are painted #F6841F, which appears in zero source files. The logo files are the mark; a config the mark never adopted cannot redefine it. The contract half-recognises this in contested_facts and then contradicts itself in success_looks_like. (2) NON-WEB MEDIA. Image-generation assets are not built from Tailwind — the contract's own argument concedes nothing about them — and neither are the email templates (Arial by design in lib/notifications/templates/, because webfonts do not survive email clients) nor print (no CMYK or Pantone token exists anywhere). Extending token authority to media that never consumed tokens is an unearned generalisation. (3) THE MARKETING/UI DISTINCTION is exactly what the evidence leaves open, and the contract's own #F5841E error (A1) makes the case for a deliberate marketing lineage stronger than it realised: two independent transcriptions of the mark's orange (#F5831F, and #F5841E annotated 'official' in the root layout) both sit within one unit per channel of the artwork, while #E87A1E sits 14/10/1 away. That is a pattern, not drift. WHAT THE CONTRACT SHOULD ASSERT INSTEAD: authority is per-fact-class, not global. 1) The artwork files in .design/logos/ are authoritative for the mark's own colours, geometry, casing and proportions — nothing overrides them. 2) tailwind.config.ts is authoritative for what any named token resolves to, always and without exception. 3) DESIGN.md + tailwind.config.ts + app/globals.css are authoritative for web and product-UI colour, type and role, and where they disagree with the brand guideline the guideline is stale (navy, Manrope/Inter, #F9FAFB, #AE5B16 all settled this way). 4) For print, email, and generated imagery, no production token governs; those values are a brand-owner decision that is currently unmade, and the capability must say so and escalate rather than infer them from Tailwind. 5) Any divergence between sources is surfaced with both values and their provenance and never silently resolved in either direction — including in the token direction.
